title: Night Talks in the Shadow-Play Hall
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Gu Heng（Shadow-play master Gu Heng around fifty, short gray beard, worn indigo short jacket with frayed cuffs, thick-knuckled hands, steady eyes） lifts the shadow-play hall（A village-temple side hall turned into a shadow-play hall; white cloth screen hung under the beam, tung-oil lamps and rod racks behind the screen, wooden floor worn deep by footsteps） back curtain and checks the rod rack behind the white cloth screen.

A row of five tung-oil lamps（A row of five tung-oil lamps hanging under the shadow-play hall beam, brass pans polished bright, wicks neat） hangs under the shadow-play hall beam; Gu Heng tops up oil and straightens each wick.

Two call-to-stage bells（Two call-to-stage copper bells hung under the shadow-play hall eaves, red cords on the clappers, ringing clear when wind rises） hang under the shadow-play hall eaves; Gu Heng reaches up and lets them tinkle softly.
Gu Heng hangs the Guan Gong shadow puppet on a rod and tests the blade-arm joint tightness.
Through a gap in the white cloth screen Gu Heng watches the village road darken outside.

The Guan Gong shadow puppet（A half-person-tall Guan Gong leather shadow puppet, red face, green robe, vivid gold armor, holding a Green Dragon Crescent Blade, joints laced with silk thread）'s red face and green robe stand vivid in the lamplight; the blade tip trembles lightly.
Gu Heng sits against a prop chest and listens to frogs outside the hall.

Gu Heng draws the chest-bottom playbook（A thread-bound old playbook, earth-yellow cover lettered 'Flooding the Seven Armies', fuzzy page edges, neat ink） from the bottom of a black-lacquer prop chest and spreads it on his knees.
With charcoal Gu Heng marks tonight's gong cues for 'Flooding the Seven Armies' in the playbook blanks.
Gu Heng closes the playbook and tucks it back into the chest lining.
A tung-oil lamp behind the screen flickers; the Guan Gong shadow puppet's blade shadow sweeps Gu Heng's cheek.

At the morning village drying ground（A tamped-earth drying ground at the village mouth, chili strings drying all around, poplars and earthen courtyards in the distance）, Gu Heng greets young A-Tang（Young A-Tang: a lean shadow-play apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, ochre-red cloth strip at the nape, patched blue tunic, bright stubborn eyes） pushing the vermilion cart prop chests（A vermilion-painted two-wheeled cart stacked with three black-lacquer prop chests, lids studded with copper corners）.
A-Tang stops the cart prop chests at the drying-ground edge and wedges the wheels with wood.

Gu Heng points to the three leather shadow nails（Three thumb-long painted leather shadow nails hung on hemp rope on a drying-ground post, heads dotted in different colors） on the post and teaches A-Tang to read color dots and play routes.
A-Tang squats by the drying-ground earth ridge and curiously touches dew on the chili strings.
Gu Heng pats A-Tang's shoulder and explains tonight's entrance-exit cues for the shadow-play hall.
A-Tang looks back at the vermilion cart prop chests, eyes full of longing.

In the temple-fair lane（A narrow stone lane at the temple fair; bamboo awnings on both sides, lanterns mixed with the smell of sugar figures）, A-Che（A-Che, whose face closely resembles young A-Tang's, ochre-green cloth strip at the nape, swaggering look, a brass shadow nail by the ear） with the ochre-green cloth strip turns from behind a sugar-figure stall.
A-Che strides across the lane's stone slabs, swaggering.
A-Che brushes past a woman selling incense; the brass shadow nail by his ear flashes.
A-Che turns into the crowd and vanishes deep among the temple-fair lanterns.
On the village drying ground A-Tang and A-Che stand side by side—one ochre-red cloth strip, one ochre-green.
A-Tang hands a picked-up shadow nail to A-Che; they lock eyes briefly.
A-Che tidies A-Tang's ochre-red cloth strip, then turns his face away.
They part at the drying-ground earth ridge and walk opposite ways.
Months later at night, Gu Heng keeps watch alone in the shadow-play hall; the Guan Gong shadow puppet hangs on its rod.

Gu Heng opens the chest-bottom playbook（The same playbook blackened by tung-oil lamp smoke on the cover, characters yellowed and blurred, corners scorched and wrinkled）; the cover is blackened by tung-oil lamp smoke, corners scorched and wrinkled.
Gu Heng wipes soot from the Guan Gong shadow puppet's green robe with a cloth.
Through a gap in the white cloth screen Gu Heng watches the pitch-black village road.
The Guan Gong shadow puppet's blade shadow sways slowly on the cloth screen.
At spring-festival season Gu Heng rehearses day after day in the shadow-play hall.
On a high-summer afternoon Gu Heng wipes the sun-hot rod rack.
On the eve of the autumn temple fair Gu Heng alone cues blade points behind the screen.
Another New Year's Eve, Gu Heng keeps the tung-oil lamps till dawn.
At dawn Gu Heng patrols the village drying ground; the vermilion cart prop chests sit under the poplars.
Gu Heng crouches to check the shaft tenons of the cart prop chests.
Gu Heng walks to the post; those earlier three leather shadow nails still hang on the hemp rope.

A strange green-hide cart（A strange green-hide cart with denser spokes and iron-sheeted bed—nothing like the vermilion cart prop chests） rolls across the drying ground—denser spokes, not the vermilion cart prop chests.
Gu Heng stands at the drying-ground edge noting temple-fair footprints ebbing away like a tide.
Gu Heng folds the dried screen cloth and weights it on a drying-ground stone pier.
Fire breaks at midnight; sparks spray from the shadow-play hall beam; the Guan Gong shadow puppet shakes hard.
Flames lick the white cloth screen; pale smoke-light fills the hall.

With a crack, a fissure bursts across the Guan Gong shadow puppet（The same Guan Gong puppet: a crack bursts across the chest, green-robe hide curled up, blade joint loose, shadow incomplete）'s chest; the blade-arm joint comes loose.
On the drying ground outside, the vermilion cart prop chests are caught by flying fire tongues.

The cart prop chests（The vermilion cart collapsed in fire, shafts charred black, chests broken apart, only twisted iron-hoop wreckage left） collapse with a roar; shafts charred black, chests broken into wreckage.
Gu Heng rushes into the shadow-play hall and clutches the cracked Guan Gong shadow puppet hard.
Next morning Gu Heng stands before the ruined screen of the shadow-play hall, staring at the cracked Guan Gong shadow puppet.
Gu Heng strokes the crack on the Guan Gong shadow puppet's chest with a fingertip, expression darkened.
At the wall base inside the hall Gu Heng charcoal-notes the date the cart prop chests caught fire.
An old photo of the cart prop chests is still nailed to the shadow-play hall wall; Gu Heng gazes a long time.
Gu Heng takes down one of the five tung-oil lamps from the beam and sits alone by its faint light.
The damaged Guan Gong shadow puppet still hangs on its rod; the blade shadow has a gap.
Weeks later Gu Heng brings leather and dye and begins mending the Guan Gong shadow puppet.

From a wood box Gu Heng takes a replica small puppet（A half-foot-tall replica Guan Gong puppet, similar pose but no gold armor, blade of bamboo, black-wood base）—posed like Guan Gong but without gold armor, blade of bamboo.
Gu Heng carefully stitches a leather patch onto the Guan Gong shadow puppet and re-threads the blade-arm silk.

The last crack is filled; the Guan Gong shadow puppet（The Guan Gong puppet's crack is stitched with a leather patch, green robe recolored, joints re-threaded, blade shadow whole again）'s green robe and gold armor shine vivid again.
The repaired Guan Gong shadow puppet's blade shadow is whole; Gu Heng breathes out.

A blue-gray replica cart（A blue-gray two-wheeled cart with a lower bed, no vermilion paint, no copper-corner chests—only firewood bundles） rolls onto the drying ground—lower bed, nothing like the long-burned cart prop chests.

County troupe steward（A lean county troupe steward in an indigo long robe and skullcap, build close to Gu Heng's, but a county crest embroidered on the cuff） jumps down from the cart and talks beside Gu Heng; the two builds are close.
The steward points at the replica cart and explains the county's temporary grain-hauling loan.
The replica cart rumble-rolls away; Gu Heng alone watches it leave the drying ground.

Into the temple-fair lane comes a sugar-figure girl（A girl selling sugar figures at the temple fair, light-brown cloth strip, gray tunic; at a glance like young A-Tang, but sharper chin and shy eyes） with a light-brown cloth strip; at a glance she somewhat resembles young A-Tang.
The girl tries handing over sugar figures, but Gu Heng shakes his head—she is not A-Tang after all.

Years later at dusk, white-haired Gu Heng（The same master's twilight look: hair and beard white, right leg slightly lame, leaning on a boxwood cane, indigo short jacket faded to gray-blue） leans on a boxwood cane under the blue-brick old opera stage（An abandoned blue-brick opera stage east of the village; two looking-posts missing at the lip, fallen leaves on the boards）.
Leaning on the cane Gu Heng looks up at the broken looking-posts, gaze distant.
Those two call-to-stage bells at the old opera stage eaves corner ring lightly in the wind; Gu Heng stops on his cane to listen.
Gu Heng presses his palm to the cold blue brick of the stage, as if saying goodbye.

By day, adult A-Tang（Adult A-Tang: a young master in his twenties with broad shoulders and steady hands, still wearing the ochre-red cloth strip, blue tunic swapped for a fitted short jacket, calm eyes） returns along the village road and hurries toward the old opera stage.
Under the old opera stage A-Tang reunites with cane-leaning Gu Heng; they embrace.
Beside the sickbed in the shadow-play hall, A-Tang holds Gu Heng's withered hand.
Gu Heng（The master has closed his eyes in death, lying still beside the prop chests, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies.
Behind the shadow-play hall door Gu Heng's indigo short jacket still hangs; A-Tang reaches to stroke it lightly.

By the shadow-play hall lintel, adult A-Tang stands before the master's brass plaque（A brass plaque nailed to the shadow-play hall lintel, engraved 'Gu's Shadow Play' and a year, verdigris on the edges）.
A-Tang's fingertip traces Gu Heng's name engraved on the plaque.

Adult A-Che（Adult A-Che still wears the ochre-green cloth strip and brass shadow nail by the ear; broader shoulders, deeper expression） arrives from a neighboring village and locks eyes with A-Tang under the old opera stage.
A-Tang and A-Che stand side by side at the stage lip—one calm-eyed, one deep-faced.
They look at each other in silence, studying faces alike yet different.
The shot returns to years ago—the youth who wedged the cart wheels on the drying ground appears again.
The opening moment returns—behind the shadow-play hall screen, a red-faced green-robed puppet is hung on a rod for the first time.
Flash to that year's temple fair—the figure with ochre-green cloth strip and brass shadow nail by the ear flickers past.
Again that row of five old tung-oil lamps under the shadow-play hall beam appears.
Back to the tamped-earth drying ground of first meeting; chili strings sway in the wind as before.
A-Tang reopens that smoke-stained chest-bottom playbook and walks into the shadow-play hall.
By the drying-ground post, those earlier three leather shadow nails still hang on the hemp rope.
A-Tang takes the Guan Gong shadow puppet's rod; the blade shadow falls on the white cloth screen again.
